faq.q: Do I need to connect my wallet?
faq.a: No. Balances are public on the blockchain, so any address can be checked without connecting or signing anything.

faq.q: Where do the balances and prices come from?
faq.a: Balances are read from the blockchain itself. USD prices are also read on-chain, from PancakeSwap and Uniswap pools with enough liquidity (at least $5,000 on the quote side). Tokens without such a pool are listed but not counted in the total.

Scammers send worthless tokens to many wallets, often with a website in the name, to lure people to fake sites. CRYPY hides tokens that look like this and shows the reason. Never visit links in token names.

faq.q: Why does the value differ from my wallet app?
faq.a: Wallet apps may use other price sources, update at different times, or include tokens without a reliable on-chain price. CRYPY never guesses a price.
Ethereum and BNB Chain. The same address can hold different coins and tokens on each chain, so both are shown.

unit-converter.name: Unit Converter
unit-converter.question: How many gwei is this?
unit-converter.description: Convert between wei, gwei and ETH or BNB exactly, without rounding.
features: Wei, gwei and ETH or BNB, both ways
Exact to the last wei, no rounding
Runs in your browser
howTo: Type an amount into any box: wei, gwei or ETH / BNB.
The other two boxes update instantly with the exact value.
Use the copy button next to a value to copy it.

faq.a: Wei is the smallest unit of ETH: 1 ETH equals 1,000,000,000,000,000,000 wei (10^18). BNB on BNB Chain uses the same 18 decimals, so the same units apply to BNB.
One gwei is 1,000,000,000 wei (10^9), or 0.000000001 ETH. Gas prices are usually quoted in gwei.

faq.q: How do I work out a transaction fee?
faq.a: Multiply the gas used by the gas price. For example, a simple transfer using 21,000 gas at 20 gwei costs 420,000 gwei, which is 0.00042 ETH.

faq.q: Do tokens use the same units?
faq.a: Not always. Many tokens use 18 decimals like ETH, but some don't: USDT on Ethereum uses 6 decimals, while USDT on BNB Chain uses 18. Check the token's decimals before converting token amounts.

faq.q: Is anything I type sent to a server?
faq.a: No. The conversion runs entirely in your browser.

hex-converter.name: Hex Converter
hex-converter.question: What number is this hex value?
hex-converter.description: Convert hexadecimal and decimal values used on blockchains, up to 256 bits.
features: Hex to decimal and back
32-byte form, byte length and signed reading
Shows text hidden in hex data
Runs in your browser
howTo: Paste a hex value (with or without 0x) or a decimal number.
See the decimal, hex and 32-byte forms instantly.
For digits-only input, choose whether it is decimal or hex.

faq.a: The EVM works with 32-byte words, and node APIs return numbers such as block numbers, balances and gas in hexadecimal (for example 0x10 = 16).
The value padded to 64 hex digits. This is how numbers appear in transaction data and contract storage.
Contracts can store signed numbers (int256) using two's complement. When a 32-byte value starts with the top bit set, it represents a negative number, shown here.

faq.q: What is the largest value supported?
faq.a: 2^256 − 1, the largest number an EVM uint256 can hold.

address-formatter.name: Address Formatter
address-formatter.question: Is this address written correctly?
address-formatter.description: Check that an address is written correctly and get its checksummed form. Works for one address or a list.
features: Detects typing mistakes using the EIP-55 checksum
Checks up to 500 addresses at once
Works for every EVM chain
Runs in your browser
howTo: Paste one address, or a list with one address per line.
Each address is marked as correct, unprotected (no checksum) or mistyped.
Copy the checksummed form of correct addresses.

faq.a: EIP-55 mixes upper- and lower-case letters in an address to encode a check. If you mistype a character, the check almost always fails, so the mistake is caught before you send anything.
Yes. It is the same address, but it carries no checksum, so a typing mistake could go unnoticed. The checksummed form adds that protection.

faq.q: What should I do if the checksum is wrong?
faq.a: Don't use the address. A wrong checksum means a character was changed. Copy the address again from its original source; don't try to fix it by hand.

faq.q: Is the address the same on Ethereum and BNB Chain?
faq.a: All EVM chains use the same address format, so the same address can exist on each of them, but balances and contracts differ per chain. Exchange deposit addresses often accept only one network, so always check which network the recipient supports.

faq.q: Does a correct address mean it is safe?
faq.a: No. It only means the address is written correctly. Use CRYPY's search to see what the address is before sending to it.

tx-decoder.name: Transaction Data Decoder
tx-decoder.question: What does this transaction data mean?
tx-decoder.description: Turn raw transaction data into a readable function and values, with warnings for risky approvals.
features: Decodes common token, NFT, router and ownership functions
Warns about unlimited approvals and NFT operator approvals
Decodes calls inside multicall
Runs in your browser
howTo: Copy the transaction's input data (it starts with 0x) from a block explorer or your wallet's data view.
Paste it here; it is decoded instantly.
Read the function, its values and any warnings before you confirm a transaction.

faq.a: The input data tells a contract what to do. The first 4 bytes (the function selector) identify the function, and the rest holds its values in 32-byte words.
On a block explorer, open the transaction and look for Input Data (view it as the original hex). Many wallets also show the hex data in an advanced or data tab before you confirm.
It lets the spender move any amount of that token from your wallet, now and in the future, until you revoke it. If the spender is malicious or later hacked, those tokens can be taken.

faq.q: Why does it say unknown function?
faq.a: CRYPY only decodes a list of well-known functions and never guesses. Different functions can share the same selector, so guessing could show you the wrong meaning.
Amounts are in the token's smallest unit. Divide by 10 to the power of the token's decimals, or use the Unit Converter for 18-decimal tokens.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
body: CRYPY never asks for, collects or stores seed phrases, recovery phrases or private keys.
Addresses and transaction hashes you search are public blockchain data. CRYPY does not store them, except addresses you choose to save to a watchlist after signing in.
Your language and theme choices are saved in your browser only.
Full details, including any analytics and third-party services, will be listed here before launch.

terms.title: Terms of Use
body: CRYPY provides information tools for public blockchain data. It does not hold, move or manage your funds.
You are responsible for every transaction you confirm in your own wallet.
Full terms will be published here before launch.

risk.title: Risk Disclosure
body: Crypto assets are risky. Prices can fall to zero and transactions cannot be reversed.
CRYPY's security checks show signals from automated tools and data providers. No check can prove that a token, contract or wallet is safe.
Nothing on CRYPY is financial, legal or tax advice. Always do your own research.
